decision.detail: I pull the chair up to the patch. The chair is the one I dragged in earlier, the one with the broken caster that drags a thin black line across the concrete. I sit. The patch is warm, the little red light on the send button pulsing slow, waiting. I pick up the handset. I dial the Pittsburgh number from the back of my notebook, the one Alma gave me in pencil, not the one in the station directory. I press send. I hold the handset to my ear. I wait. The line hums, a low electrical thrum, and then it clears. The file is moving. I set the handset down. I do not write a slug. I do not attach a memo. I stand. I walk past the dark projector room where the reel Larry took is already gone, past the smell of hot dust and baked celluloid that still hangs in the air. I walk out the side door. February air hits my face. The ballroom lights are on across the street, a warm rectangle in the dark. I do not go over. I do not go to the ballroom. I do not open my notebook. I walk. The street is empty. My boots make a small sound on the wet pavement. I walk until the station lights are behind me and I cannot see them anymore. I do not call anyone. I do not explain. I walk home.
decision.intention: One voice, one daughter, one machine that will not run a forty-third winter. The file is moving through the regional line right now, unslugged, untitled, unbranded. It is not a story. It is not a segment. It is a mother talking to her kid across a wire, and it is the only clean copy that will ever exist because the reel Larry kept is his and the patch I used is mine and the machine in this room is done. I sent it because the line was open and I was here and the window is closing and I am not going to be the person who sat in the ballroom dancing while the only recording of Alma's voice moved through a queue overnight and got lost in a server. I sent it. That is the act. I am walking home and I am not going back.
decision.words: None. I do not say it to Phil. I do not say it to Larry. I do not say it to the station. The hum in the handset was enough. I am silent on the street and I will be silent for the rest of the night and that is not a failure, that is the whole point.
